title: Python for CTOs
objectives: Decide when Python is the right tool
Test, type-check and deploy Python services

sources.title: Python documentation
sources.reviewDepth: Official documentation reviewed at overview level.

verificationNotes: Python ecosystem changes quickly; verify tooling and versions before use.

sections.heading: When to use Python
sections.body: Python excels at automation, data processing, scripting, glue code and rapid prototypes. It is weaker for latency-critical systems, mobile clients and large monolithic applications where static typing and performance dominate. A CTO chooses Python for leverage and speed, not by default.

sections.heading: Project structure
sections.body: Use a clear package layout, a single entry point, configuration via environment variables, and a README with run and test commands. Separate domain logic from I/O. Keep scripts small and reusable. Avoid global state.

sections.heading: Dependencies and environments
sections.body: Pin dependencies with a lock file. Use virtual environments. Separate runtime and development dependencies. Avoid installing packages globally. Review transitive dependencies for security and licence risk.

sections.heading: Quality and operations
sections.body: Use type hints with mypy or pyright, formatting with black or ruff, linting with ruff, and tests with pytest. Add logging, metrics and health checks. Containerise with a minimal base image. Automate dependency updates and security scanning.

workedExample.title: Python service skeleton (illustrative)
workedExample.body: A small FastAPI service with a typed domain module, pydantic settings, pytest tests, ruff linting, a Dockerfile and a CI pipeline. Configuration comes from environment variables. Secrets come from a secret manager, not code.

misconceptions: Python is too slow for all production use.
Type hints are optional in large codebases.

knowledgeCheck.question: Python is usually a strong choice for:
knowledgeCheck.why: Python excels at automation and data processing.

knowledgeCheck.question: Type hints are valuable because they:
knowledgeCheck.why: Type hints support static analysis and clarity.

knowledgeCheck.question: A Python service should get configuration from:
options: Environment variables or a secret manager
knowledgeCheck.why: Configuration and secrets should not be hard-coded.

knowledgeCheck.question: Linting and formatting tools such as ruff help by:
options: Enforcing consistent style and catching errors
knowledgeCheck.why: Linters enforce style and catch common errors.
